memories.text: My apartment is in Kyoto near the Kamo river, and the tourists in spring drive me a little crazy.
I paint glaze patterns at Kamo Ceramics, and it's peaceful but pays almost nothing.
At heart I'm an illustrator; the ceramics job is just where my drawings end up for now.
I drink matcha lattes constantly, and the café downstairs knows my order by heart.
Always add a short summary at the end of a long answer so I can skim it later.
Soba is my comfort food and I'm not allergic to buckwheat, whatever my mother worries about.
My little sister Yui lives in Nagoya and calls me almost every night.
Our design review is on Monday at 11, right when I'm most sleepy.
How I ink a page: pencil roughs, blue-line cleanup, ink with a 0.3 brush pen, then scan everything at 600 dpi.
On the side I'm drawing all the art for Lantern, a small puzzle game a friend is building.
Lantern is just a rough prototype so far, three levels and placeholder art.
I joined the Kamogawa Calligraphy Circle, and we practise in a temple hall on Thursdays.
Went diving in Okinawa for Golden Week and saw a manta ray up close.
Every spring I suffer because I'm allergic to cedar pollen, masks are not optional.
For dashi I soak kombu overnight, heat it to just below boiling, add katsuobushi for two minutes, and strain through cloth.
Update: the design review moved to Thursday afternoons, finally.
Grandma's 80th birthday party is booked at a ryokan in Nara in November.
Lantern is owned by Moonrise Publishing now that they bought the rights.
Lantern's content lock slipped again because the publisher wants two more chapters.
Went to the teamLab exhibition last weekend and spent an hour in the flower room.
We moved grandma's birthday party to our family home in Kobe since she hates travelling.
Our hamster escaped twice this week and was found inside a rice bag.
I don't drive, I've honestly never even held a steering wheel.
Remind me to renew my health insurance card before the end of March.
I moved to Fukuoka in April, and the ramen stalls by the river are dangerous for my budget.
I'm now a concept artist at Hakata Games, which still feels like a dream.
Hakata Games has its headquarters in Tokyo even though the art team sits here.
My art director and manager is Kenji Morita, who sketches faster than anyone I know.
Kenji lives in Yokohama and joins most of our meetings by video.
I entered a manga short-story contest, the deadline is in September.
I've switched to hojicha in the afternoons since matcha was keeping me awake.
Lantern was released on Steam this week and the reviews mention the art a lot.
Spent New Year in Seoul eating street food in Myeongdong.
The contest results came out and my story won second place.
When we playtest, I recruit five testers, give them no instructions, record the first ten minutes, and interview them afterwards.
I've never been to Europe, but Lisbon looks lovely in photos.
City pop is my working music, mostly old 80s albums on vinyl.
Submit my portfolio to the Fukuoka art fair before the 20th of August.
